hazard: Lack of system to ensure communication between treating consultants
theme: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

reports.title: Sheila Ridgway
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

concerns.quote: Communication between speciality consultants ~ lack of any system to ensure that communication occurs between the treating consultants as to the necessity for identifying and documenting any potential ongoing risks when speciality specific treatments are being contemplated or planned for the different specialities simultaneously
concerns.hazard: lack of system to ensure communication between treating consultants

reports.title: Thomas Gibson: Prevention of future deaths report
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

promises.quote: we have focused on the Human Factors of errors in clinical medicine and have engaged with our Human Factors Academy (HFA). This will support us to understand better the other factors at play which contribute to incorrect ECG interpretation; and which can be mitigated in the future. 1
promises.summary: Engage Human Factors Academy to mitigate ECG interpretation errors

concerns.quote: a narrow focus on the error of three different doctors to interpret two ECGs correctly (rather than any broader consideration of the context in which such misinterpretations occurred) represents a missed opportunity to fully understand the factors that led to Mr [name redacted] discharge from hospital, thus creating a risk of future deaths
concerns.hazard: misinterpretation of ECG results leading to missed diagnosis

concerns.quote: there does not appear to be clear guidance available to those working within the Trust as to what is required when communicating (particularly as to test results and a patient's presentation) as between different specialisms and as between different roles within the team
concerns.hazard: lack of communication guidance across specialties and roles

concerns.quote: there is no specific guidance as to expected minimum standards as to obtaining appropriate context / information for clinicians (whether from the HIVE system or otherwise) when asked to review a single test or investigation result in isolation
concerns.hazard: inadequate contextual information for test review

concerns.quote: there does not currently appear to be any particular requirement in place for a senior review of the patient to take place in circumstances where diagnostic tests undertaken yield results which appear incongruous / unexpected in the context of their presentation
concerns.hazard: missing senior review for incongruous test results

concerns.quote: no wider audit of ECGs interpreted in the Emergency Department / Acute Medical Unit prior to discharge of patients appears to have been undertaken
concerns.hazard: absence of ECG audit before discharge

concerns.quote: no audit as to the sufficiency of detail contained in discharge summaries appears to have been undertaken to date in the light of the issues identified by the Trust's High Impact Learning Assessment

links.explanation: Both reports highlight insufficient mechanisms for effective communication between different medical specialties within the trust. The earlier report notes a missing system for sharing risk information, while the later report points to absent clear guidance on communicating test results and patient presentations across specialisms and roles.
links.earlier_quote: Communication between speciality consultants ~ lack of any system to ensure that communication occurs between the treating consultants as to the necessity for identifying and documenting any potential ongoing risks
links.later_quote: there does not appear to be clear guidance available to those working within the Trust as to what is required when communicating (particularly as to test results and a patient's presentation) as between different specialisms and as between different roles within the team.
